So, in reading this SCP, my first question is what happens if a humanoid that has no need to eat/can't eat opens the book? Its likely the Foundation would choose a subject that is rather docile. Additionally, if this subject is already at Site-19 (where SCP-241 is kept), you can save most costs of transport. Such an SCP can be found in SCP-1770. As such, I am proposing the following addendum:

Addendum 3: Notes from Crosstesting:
To determine the effects of SCP-241's recipes on subjects that either cannot eat or do not require sustenance, approval was given to crosstest SCP-241 on SCP-1770. Upon subject opening the book, the contents were identical to before it was closed previously. This confirms results of Test 241-23, ██/██/20██, in which SCP-241 does not respond to inorganic subjects.

Such a crosslink could also be added to the experiment log supplement page associated with this article.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
Re Subject-241-C
Subjects 241-C and 241-D were chosen from general population
So she's not Class-D, not some felon or something.
Subject balked at eating the dish, saying that “it smells like ████,” but was persuaded to eat it by [DATA EXPUNGED]. Subject ate approximately 40% of the meal before stating, “I’m gonna be sick,” at which time subject vomited. Subject was instructed to finish the meal, but subject responded [DATA EXPUNGED]. Termination of subject considered but rejected in favor of further testing.
So she is some woman taken off the street, who says she can't cook, forced to cook and eat something which makes her sick, they try to force her to eat more and almost terminate her for not doing so.
Downvoted until this is resolved…even for the Foundation, that is sick.

item.content:encoded:
This one is from 2008, so it really pre-dates current site culture. That said, most of those can be easily resolved, as shown below:

"(see Document [DATA EXPUNGED])"
==>
"(see Document invent-a-serial-number)"

"Any anomalies must be reported immediately to [DATA EXPUNGED]."
==>
"Any anomalies must be reported immediately to (someone in charge)"

"Access to SCP-241 is restricted by four guards armed with [DATA EXPUNGED]."
==>
"Access to SCP-241 is restricted."

"Any and all usage of SCP-241 must be logged, including [DATA EXPUNGED]."
==>
" Any and all usage of SCP-241 must be logged."

"Whenever possible, dishes prepared from SCP-241 should be cooked by ████ ███████ (Subject 241-F)"
==>
Actually, I don't like this bit at all, since the whole point of this SCP is how its effect is personalized.

"Anyone who opens SCP-241 outside of a testing environment must immediately report to the nearest infirmary as well as [DATA EXPUNGED]."
==>
This one is…. hm. If you open 241, it attunes itself to you and then starts giving you food allergies. So if you open it by mistake, then you should a) report to an infirmary, and b) …. have a D-class close and re-open it?

item.content:encoded: Possible um… plot hole, for lack of a better term: the book specifically provides recipe that will prove fatal to the person who opened it, right? So how come the old woman who owned it had it in her possession for so long? Did she genuinely NEVER eat ANYTHING made from a recipe in that book after she opened it personally? Considering that she had it through three marriages, that seems unlikely to me. And yes, I know it says she kept the book open and on a stand, but the only way I can see this working is if it was given to her by someone else, probably in her own kitchen, while it was already open, after which point it went immdiately onto the stand.
